etymologies.etymologyHTML: From rely +‎ -ance.

definitions.definition: The act of relying (on or in someone or something); trust.

quote.citation: c. 1605–1608, William Shakespeare, “The Life of Tymon of Athens”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act II, scene i]:
quote.text: […]  his days and times are pastAnd my reliances on his fracted [i.e. broken] datesHave smit my credit:

quote.citation: 1752, Charlotte Lennox, The Female Quixote‎[1], London: A. Millar, Volume 2, Book 9, Chapter 9, p. 288:
quote.text: How unfavourable is Chance, said Arabella fretting at the Disappointment, to Persons who have any Reliance upon it!

quote.citation: 1867, Thomas Babington Macaulay, “Samuel Johnson”, in Biographical and Historical Sketches‎[2], New York: Appleton, page 54:
quote.text: It was out of his power to support his son at either university; but a wealthy neighbor offered assistance; and, in reliance on promises which proved to be of very little value, Samuel was entered at Pembroke College, Oxford.

quote.citation: 1912, W. Somerset Maugham, Mrs. Dot‎[3], London: Heinemann, act 2, page 89:
quote.text: I put infinite reliance in your tact.

quote.citation: 1962, C. S. Forester, chapter 3, in Hornblower and the Hotspur‎[4], London: Michael, Joseph:
quote.text: Hornblower could see in a flash that he could place implicit reliance on Bush’s seamanship.

definitions.definition: The condition of being reliant or dependent.

quote.text: […]  he contended that habitual reliance on engine power causes a pilot to lose his ability to make a forced landing “deadstick” if necessary.

quote.citation: 2016 July 20, Roger Wilkins, “Australia’s economic wellbeing is at a standstill as rift between young and old widens”, in The Guardian:
quote.text: Poverty in Australia has declined, welfare reliance has stabilised and long-term poverty is becoming rare—but overall economic wellbeing is no longer improving  […]

definitions.definition: (dated) Anything on which to rely; ground of trust.

quote.citation: 1593, Thomas Nashe, Christs Teares ouer Ierusalem‎[5], London: Thomas Thorp, published 1613, page 69:
quote.text: Thou wert once the chiefe pillar of my posterity, and the whole reliance of my name:

quote.citation: 1656, Robertson Sanderson, Twenty Sermons‎[6], London: Henry Seile, Sermon 14, p. 280:
quote.text: A horse is counted but a vain thing,  […]  to save a man. So are Chariots, and Forts, and Armies, and Navies, and all earthly reliances.

quote.citation: 1741, [Samuel Richardson], “Letter XXXII”, in Pamela: Or, Virtue Rewarded. […], volume (please specify |volume=I to IV), London:  […]  C[harles] Rivington, […]; and J. Osborn, […], →OCLC, page 286:
quote.text: Mr. Adams may marry as well as Mr. Williams; and both, I believe, will find God’s Providence a better Reliance, than the richest Benefice in England.

quote.citation: 1914, Stephen Leacock, chapter 5, in Adventurers of the Far North‎[7], Toronto: Glasgow, Brook, page 123:
quote.text: Most ominous of all was the discovery of over six hundred empty cans that had held preserved meat, the main reliance of the expedition.

definitions.definition: A person or thing which relies on another. (The addition of quotations indicative of this usage is being sought:)
